name: Discrete Ray-Marching with Forward Scattering Approximation
definition: A rendering pass that projects the cloud onto the frame buffer using ray-marching, accounting for reflection and scattering. It approximates forward light-scattering density by assuming 50% of light scatters in the forward direction within a small solid angle (~0.0001 steradians), ignoring the remaining 50% to save computation.
summary: Discrete Ray-Marching with Forward Scattering Approximation is a real-time volumetric rendering method that discretizes light propagation and assumes 50% of scattered light moves forward, ignoring the rest to reduce computational cost.
